messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=network-edge-lb-health severity=page - on-call: jordan
jordan: ack. I'm on it. seeing increased TLS handshake failures and client 502s in us-west-2.
maya: jumping in. any console screenshots?
samir: pulling target health now. running: 
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:us-west-2:xxxx:targetgroup/edge-prod/abcd1234
```
samir: result: 1/4 healthy, others failing with `TLS alert (bad certificate)` and `SSL routines:ssl3_get_server_certificate:certificate verify failed`
lucas: we did a cert rotation earlier for the ALB. Did the node config get a rollback? I saw a config rollback event at ~08:05 UTC in deploy-log.
jordan: possible SNI/cert mismatch. maya, can you verify the cert presented by the backends vs what ALB expects?
maya: doing `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood-inference.example.com` -> returns cert CN `internal-edge.local` and issuer `Redwood Internal CA` (not the public cert). looks like the host has stale internal cert.
customer-support: we're getting a spike of tickets: "TLS handshake failed", multiple customers in APAC and EU routing through us-west-2 are affected. estimated impact ~12-18% of traffic.
jordan: ok. mitigation plan options: a) deregister bad targets from TG to stop handshake failures b) push correct cert to nodes (rolling) c) shift Route53 weights away from us-west-2 temporarily. quick fav?
lucas: deregister is fastest. I'll coordinate with Samir to identify failing IPs. also check ASG to prevent immediate replacement with bad nodes.
samir: failing ip list: 10.0.5.12, 10.0.5.13. healthy: 10.0.5.14, 10.0.5.15. deregistering 10.0.5.12/13 now. cmd: 
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=10.0.5.12 Id=10.0.5.13
```
samir: done. ALB shows 2/4 healthy now. traffic will be shifted to healthy nodes.
maya: I'll start rolling cert push to the two bad hosts. runbook: 
```
1) scp cert bundle to /etc/ssl/edge.pem
2) sudo chown root:ssl && chmod 640 /etc/ssl/edge.pem
3) systemctl restart edge-proxy
4) verify with curl --resolve and openssl s_client
```
maya: starting deploy to 10.0.5.12 (will be quick).
jordan: pagerduty, escalate to eng-lead for customer comms.
pagerduty: Escalation: notification sent to hilary. Incident acknowledged by jordan.
customer-support: drafting status page: "We are investigating partial TLS handshake failures affecting some API requests routed via us-west-2. Engineers are removing affected hosts and restoring certificates. Service is partially degraded." Will post on signoff.
lucas: note: autoscale launched a replacement at 09:10 UTC but user-data had previous cert state due to a failed config-update job. need idempotent config step in ASG lifecycle.
samir: re-check: 10.0.5.12 now presents correct CN after cert push. re-registering into target group.
samir: cmd: 
```
aws elbv2 register-targets --target-group-arn <arn> --targets Id=10.0.5.12 Id=10.0.5.13
```
samir: describe-target-health -> 4/4 healthy, healthchecks passing (HTTPS).
jordan: great. customer-support, ready to post update that mitigation completed and we're monitoring?
customer-support: posted: "Mitigation applied — affected hosts removed and certificates corrected. All targets healthy as of 09:28 UTC. Monitoring for 30 minutes. No data loss reported." Notified paying customers.
incident-bot: Incident resolved by jordan. Automated tasks created: postmortem ticket assigned to eng-runtime, and eng-security pinged to review rotation process.
jordan: leaving postmortem owner to maya. I'll stay on-call for 30 minutes in case of regressions.
maya: creating postmortem: timeline + root cause: partial config rollback left internal cert on edge hosts; gap in ASG config rollout and pre-deploy SNI verification. Action items: add preflight SNI cert check in deploy pipeline, prevent rollback from reverting cert bundle, add ALB-level synthetic TLS healthcheck.
jordan: thanks team. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
